## Current CSA State as seen on the CSA YAng model Requests

As shown before the current state picks up from the ICMP tests performed during E1 validation as the testing are being done with the same test bed and during the same session. however the CSA is not reporting any cached state as can be seen here


## End to End Evaluation: Preemption Test of ICMP Policies over HTTP Policies

### Step 1: Establish HTTP Traffic through a Python HTTP Server on Host Hotel

```console 
clab@sma-ubuntu-edge-hotel:~$ python3 -m http.server 443 --bind 0.0.0.0
Serving HTTP on 0.0.0.0 port 443 (http://0.0.0.0:443/) ...
```

The configuration done here forces port 443 in order to simulate an HTTPS server, while access is to be done through HTTP the dataset we used for training for trainig does not differentiate between HTTPS and HTTP therefore even if we serve an HTTPS server we are still going to see classification returned as HTTP

### Step 2: Establish a continuous connection from Host Golf to Host Hotel to extract validation information

```console
clab@sma-ubuntu-edge-golf:~$ for i in $(seq 1 20); do
    echo "HTTP request $i — $(date -u +%T)"
    curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code} | Time %{time_total}s\n" \
        http://192.168.20.X:443/
    sleep 3
done
```

### Step 3: Establish a Continuous HTTP client on Golf and in another terminal send ICMP Echo Request

For this section we are going to createa continuiuos bHTTP client instead of a timed one and we are going to open a second session into the application 

```console 
i=1
while true; do
    echo "HTTP request $i — $(date -u +%T)"
    curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code} | Time %{time_total}s\n" \
        http://192.168.20.10:443/
    i=$((i + 1))
    sleep 2
done
```
